| [QUESTION-287](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-287.md) | In a deterministic singularly perturbed system whose eliminated variable is fast and contracting and whose reduced system is contracting, does the memoryless quasi-steady-state reduction predict the coarse variable with an error bounded uniformly in time in terms of the eliminated dynamics? | The fast contracting case of [QUESTION-222](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-222.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-773](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-773.md) (Active) settles it. | [QUESTION-292](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-292.md) v2 | What evidence would show that a maintaining link, and not a regime's content, keeps a disorder in place: does the efficacy of a treatment that targets the link count, or only change in the link that is specific and comes before the outcome? | The evidential part of [QUESTION-045](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-045.md), split off by the status review of 2026-10-27 under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md), because [THEORY-053](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-053.md) (Active) settles it. | [QUESTION-324](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-324.md) v2 | Are the conditions an effective description is asked to meet (predictive sufficiency, dynamical independence, memory closure, approximation fidelity, tractability) of one logical kind, or are some of them parameters of the regime under which the others are assessed rather than conditions in their own right? | The last clause of [QUESTION-252](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-252.md), split off by the thirteenth status review under [ADR-049](../../../record/decisions.d/ADR-049.md) because [CLAIM-401](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-401.md) (Active) settles it: they are not of one kind. | [QUESTION-382](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-382.md) | At what interface, and under which interactions, is a system individuated as one component rather than another, when black-boxing erases internal distinctions that composition preserves and creates relations the parts lacked, and when does equivalence at an interface fail once implementation cost, maintenance or internal control is counted? | A's question, from the owner's paste of 2026-11-05 (fourth), A's "Toward a resource-sensitive Yoneda theory of individuation" §8, with the third target result of §11 and two separations of §9: "At what interface, and under which interactions, is a system individuated as one component rather than another?" The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-383](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-383.md) | Which aspects of FACT's freedom–constraint duality survive in nonlinear, stochastic, hybrid systems with endogenous constraints? | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on constraint architectures (pasted by the owner on 2026-11-04, continuing the exchange on emergency readiness whose share link could not be fetched), Part 1. | [QUESTION-386](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-386.md) | Under what funding and incentive rules does allocating resources according to observed activity cause an organization to lose capabilities whose value is concentrated in rarely encountered circumstances? | A's proposal, from the exchange on emergency readiness (2026-11-04; its share link could not be fetched, and its text was pasted by the owner), section 11 of A's "Proposed additions to Nucleation PR [#401](https://github.com/dmarx/nucleation/issues/401)". The readings show that feedback is not enough: Stern et al.'s sheet rewrites its own crease stiffnesses, but only on a supervisor's verdict. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-389](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-389.md) | Can some forms of organizational conflict be represented as internally balanced constraint loads, while others appear as missing degrees of freedom or unreachable motions? | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on constraint architectures (pasted by the owner on 2026-11-04, continuing the exchange on emergency readiness whose share link could not be fetched), Part 2. A asks whether organizational conflict splits the same way, into balanced loads within a feasible organization and missing freedoms, and says the mapping from demands to constraints "cannot simply be assumed". The record holds frustration as an empty intersection and strain as independent of it, with a dual certificate for the local residual; it has no such split. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-390](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-390.md) v2 | When origami modules are joined along shared boundaries, which constraint structures does the coupling generate, and does eliminating the interior creases leave a relation among boundary fold angles that the modules' own crease constraints can express, or one that needs higher arity, inequalities or history, and at what cost of representation and elimination? | A's question, from the owner's paste of 2026-11-05 (later), A's "Additional points of contact across the Nucleation record" §§2 and 5 and its closing experiment: classify origami assemblies "by the constraint structures generated by coupling their components", with the global configurations Q_global = {(q_1,…,q_n): φ_ij(q_i)=φ_ji(q_j)} kept apart from the physical attachment that establishes them ([TERM-093](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-093.md)); then eliminate interior creases and ask whether the boundary relation stays in the local crease vocabulary, the origami form of [QUESTION-283](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-283.md), with [THEORY-1090](../../../record/theory.d/THEORY-1090.md)'s sheaf example as the precedent; then add bounds on the representation language, the time for elimination and the cost of reconstructing the interior, and finally let the architecture change. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-391](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-391.md) | When does an effective constraint cease to be a good approximation because previously suppressed degrees of freedom become dynamically important? | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on constraint architectures (pasted by the owner on 2026-11-04, continuing the exchange on emergency readiness whose share link could not be fetched), Part 5. The time-scale form is held: [CLAIM-478](../../../record/claims.d/CLAIM-478.md) says a settled relation is a constraint over the window between two time scales, and [QUESTION-287](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-287.md), answered, bounds the error of the memoryless reduction in a contracting singularly perturbed system. What the record lacks is the energetic form. Silverberg et al.'s square twist has no rigid folding motion and folds by bending its facets: facet planarity is a constraint only below the bending energy scale, and the stiffness ratio decides whether the structure is bistable. The question asks for conditions of that kind, and whether they reduce to time-scale conditions. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-396](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-396.md) | Under what conditions does structural memory improve an organization's control over its future behavior, and when does accumulated history instead create hidden states and unexpected transition pathways? | A's proposal, from the pasted synthesis on constraint architectures (pasted by the owner on 2026-11-04, continuing the exchange on emergency readiness whose share link could not be fetched), Part 5. Memory held in configuration, as in multistable origami, can extend what a system can select, and can create states that the declared operations neither reach nor leave and that readout cannot tell apart. Jules et al.'s origami switches show both: a return-point memory over 16 states, and defect states reached only by hand, left only irreversibly, and not identified unequivocally by height and stiffness. The record holds legibility and the irreversibility of some losses; it does not ask when memory helps and when it hides. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-397](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-397.md) | Under what conditions does a partial organization increase the probability of subsequent organization by changing the transition dynamics, rather than merely providing a more advanced initial state? | A's question, verbatim, from A's review of this pull request, pasted by the owner on 2026-11-05, §5. A candidate nucleus can raise the chance of the target because establishing it puts the system in a more advanced state under the same transition rules, a state advantage. It can also change the rates of later steps among components that have not joined it, a generative architectural advantage ([TERM-117](../../../record/terms.d/TERM-117.md)). A higher committor does not tell the two apart. A's test compares matched partial assemblies, with similar completion counts, inventories and conditions, while the candidate relations are manipulated, and measures downstream reaction hazards, not only final yield. [QUESTION-380](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-380.md) asks when a small compatible subsystem helps; this asks by which of the two routes. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-398](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-398.md) v4 | Under what conditions does a partial organization become independent of the intervention that originally established it? | A's question, verbatim, from the fourth synthesis on DNA origami pasted by the owner on 2026-11-05, Prediction 6 and §10. A's test: establish a nucleus with external support, withdraw the support at matched intermediate states, and measure D(s) = q_supported(s) − q_withdrawn(s), the drop in the chance of completing when support is removed. A expects D to be large early and to approach zero once enough downstream organization has formed. A sharp fall would be an operational signature of a nucleation threshold. A separates becoming independent of the support during formation from maintenance: "The nucleus can become unnecessary while the organization it helped establish persists". The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-399](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-399.md) v2 | Under what conditions does a productive partial organization become a self-maintaining nucleus, one whose continued operation contributes to regenerating the very constraints that make its productive influence possible? | A's question, from the third synthesis on DNA origami pasted by the owner on 2026-11-05, §§7 and 10, verbatim but for the opening words. A orders the steps: a partial structure appears; it changes the dynamics so that compatible interactions become likelier; the organization comes to persist; and only under further conditions does it gain processes that replace damaged parts and regenerate its enabling constraints. "The transition from productive formation to self-maintaining organization is the most demanding step." [QUESTION-090](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-090.md) asks how a self-maintaining governance emerges from heterogeneous processes; this asks when a nucleus becomes one. The wording is A's; adopting it is the owner's call. | Open |
| [QUESTION-400](../../../record/questions.d/QUESTION-400.md) | Can changing how a fixed stock of resources is allocated among otherwise unchanged components alter which form nucleates, and so which form results, even when the set of attainable final forms stays the same? | A's question, from the synthesis on DNA origami pasted by the owner on 2026-11-05, §4: "Can changing the allocation of influence or resources among otherwise unchanged components alter which organizational form nucleates, even when the set of attainable final forms remains the same?" A grounds it in Wah et al.'s 2016 report that raising the concentration of the centre staples moves where a DNA origami rectangle starts folding; the reading shows the edge staples were cut and the total raised at the same time, so no fixed stock was reallocated. Dunn et al.'s result, filed in the same pull request, answers its molecular form in part: changing only the stability of intermediates redirects one template among final shapes of about equal free energy.
